statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 18 because the completed US cash session retraced in both directions and the evening futures session is drifting inside its range rather than extending. Stress eases to 70 as WTI falls about 3.5% toward $89 and the 2-year yield slips to 4.88% after Williams signalled no urgency, while a 30-year yield near 5.62% keeps the long end at a multi-decade high.
recommendation: Tail remains in the low band, so the mapped state stays EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The published danger window is narrow and sits on 30 September between 12:00Z and 15:00Z, where ADP, core PCE and the final Q2 GDP estimate precede the US cash open. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Cash NDX closed 30,339.33, up 0.21%, with both its opening gap and its 30,235.67 downside probe retraced; NQ 30,652.75 and VIX 16.04 hold Tail at 18, while a 5.62% 30-year yield and 81.9 consumer confidence keep Stress at 70
body:
The strongest current evidence remains the completed US cash session. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,339.33, up 62.52 points or 0.21%, from a 30,276.81 prior close. It opened at 30,412.29, printed a 30,429.97 high, sold back through the prior close to a 30,235.67 low, then recovered 103.66 points to finish green. The 194.30-point range is 0.64% of index level and, decisively for this score, retracement worked in both directions: the opening gap was retraced and the downside probe was retraced in turn. That is the structural opposite of the persistent no-retracement path Tail is designed to measure, so Tail eases to 18. The evening futures session corroborates rather than contradicts that read. NQ trades 30,652.75, up 0.28%, some 72.75 points below the 30,725.50 session high and well above the 30,372.25 low, which is range behaviour rather than extension toward an extreme. Volatility is contained at VIX 16.04, near the lower half of a 15.73 to 16.44 range.

Stress stays high at 70 for reasons that are macro rather than price-path. The 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.57% to 5.62%, its highest since 2002 to 2004, and the 10-year sits at 5.26% to 5.27%, the highest since mid-2007. The clearest development since the previous hour is a dovish repricing at the front end: New York Fed President John Williams said that after the September action there is "no need for urgency", with one further hike possibly appropriate late this year. Market-implied odds of an October increase fell to roughly 51% from about 70%, and the 2-year yield eased to 4.88%. The result is a steeper curve rather than a resolved one, which is why front-end relief does not translate into a lower Stress score. The growth side stays soft: Conference Board consumer confidence fell 6.7 points to 81.9, the weakest since April 2014, with the expectations index at 63.6, and August job openings came in near 7.1 million against a 7.23 million forecast.

Cross-assets are, on balance, supportive. WTI fell about 3.5% to roughly $89 and Brent about 2.6% to $102.59 as Saudi Arabia restored roughly half the capacity of its East-West pipeline after drone attacks, Hormuz flows continued and the US released up to 40 million barrels from emergency reserves. That is a genuine easing of the supply-side geopolitical channel, and it removes one potential Tail amplifier rather than adding one. Single-name technology news is active without being index-directional: AMD agreed to acquire Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for approximately $8.2 billion in stock, its second-largest deal ever. Shared Finviz context was read at the start of this run but its collection status was partial, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, and at roughly 105 minutes old it sat outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so it was not used to establish any current structure; the assessment rests on independently verified primary sources. No observed amplifier stack is present: volatility is contained, oil is falling, the front end is easing and the cash path retraced twice. Confidence is 88, reflecting verified index, futures, volatility, yield, oil, catalyst and calendar evidence, with the partial shared context the only material gap.

lookbackSummary: 23 of the 24 preceding hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 14:00 UTC slot on 29 September is unavailable because no assessment was published in that clock hour. Tail ranged from 17 to 24 and never left the low or watch bands. It troughed at 17 through the late Monday and early Tuesday overnight, printed 24 in the 01:00, 03:00, 04:00 and 15:00 UTC hours on trend-down readings, held 20 to 21 across the European and US cash hours, and closed the window at 19 once the US session had resolved. Stress declined steadily from 79 in the early European hours to 71 by 20:00 UTC as volatility decayed and oil fell, while Confidence held between 86 and 88 throughout. The dominant mode was mixed for most of the window, with normal readings in the overnight hours, trend-down episodes around 01:00 to 05:00 and 15:00 UTC, and a single trend-up reading at 12:00 UTC.
outlookSummary: The published forecast opens at Tail 18 for the current post-close hour, where the resolved two-way cash path and the range-bound evening futures session are actually observed, and holds 18 through the late US evening and the first Asian hours. It edges to 19 across Asian mid-morning as verified price-path evidence ages, then enters the watch band at 20 with the European pre-open and peaks at 21 around the European cash open and morning. Tail eases to 20 in the European midday lull before the pre-release build carries it to 22 in the 11:00 UTC hour and to the 24 watch ceiling for the 12:00 UTC block, where ADP, core PCE, headline PCE, personal spending and the final Q2 GDP estimate all land. The single elevated-band slot is 13:00 UTC at Tail 25, a mapped BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES state, because post-release repricing overlaps the 13:30 UTC cash open and Chicago PMI against a long end at multi-decade highs. Tail then decays to 23, 22 and 21 through the US morning and midday, returns to the 20 watch floor in the afternoon, lifts one point to 21 for the month-end power hour and settles at 20 into the close. Stress runs a shallow U from 70 down to 69 overnight and back to 75 at the release overlap before easing to 70, and Confidence declines from 88 to 82 purely as a function of distance from verified evidence. Every slot beyond the current hour is conditional risk, not observed structure.
